clue.text: Quartz found in Canadian National Park

definitions.meaning: an opaque, often red or brown, variety of the mineral used as a semi-precious stone
the large national park in the Rocky Mountains of Alberta, Canada

explanation.surface: A geologist reports a crystal discovered while hiking in a Canadian wilderness reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an impure opaque silica mineral and the park in Alberta, so two separate senses meet in one word.

clue.text: Seafood needs salt only added

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the usual crossword abbreviation for one
only, as in solely or by itself, means alone

explanation.surface: A cook insists that a seafood dish should be seasoned with nothing but salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' looks like a seasoning but it is a sailor, AB; 'added' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This edible sea snail, also called ormer, is a shellfish prized as a delicacy.

clue.text: Saintly missionary hit the hay

parts.note: to pat is to strike lightly, a gentle hit
a rick is a stack of hay

explanation.surface: A holy evangelist, worn out by his travels, finally went to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit the hay' reads as one idiom for going to bed, but it breaks into two pieces, with 'the' only a link; a rick is a stack of hay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland's patron saint was a fifth-century Christian missionary there.

clue.text: Guards, _ perhaps, processed mineral

indicators.note: something processed has been worked over and changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Security staff are seen handling an ore that has been refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processed' rearranges the letters of MINERAL. A railway guard is one example of a railway worker, so 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Train guards are among the staff who work on a railway, so they are examples of this group.

clue.text: Derivative of fish, one not seen excessively around

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something not seen is missing, so the letter for one is dropped from the word fish

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: around signals that the synonym for excessively is turned back to front

parts.note: excessively means too, as in too much

explanation.surface: An angler describes a by-product of his catch, with a single fish hidden from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derivative of fish' reads as one phrase, but the definition is only 'Derivative'; 'of' is a piece, 'not seen' drops a letter and 'around' turns the last piece back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is something that grows out of or derives from an original, like a branch.

clue.text: Fine? Just terrible!

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
just, as in fair or legitimate, means rightful

explanation.surface: Someone protests that being penalised was unfair, and simply dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a penalty or approval, but it gives F.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightful means dreadful or very bad, as of weather or behaviour.

clue.text: Rearrange beats to give new top easy time, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means this is one possible rearrangement of these letters

parts.note: C is the time signature symbol for common time in music

explanation.surface: A music teacher suggests a new, relaxed tempo for the top part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges N, TOP EASY and C. C on a stave stands for common time, four beats to the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To syncopate is to shift accents onto normally weak beats, displacing the rhythm.

clue.text: Confused us with old rose — roses generally aren't like this

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of us and old rose are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A gardener muddles an old rose variety, though most roses have a scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' rearranges US with OLD ROSE; the definition is a statement roses generally contradict.
explanation.definitionFit: Most roses have a fragrance, so lacking any smell is what they generally are not.

clue.text: Traces of drugs in alcohol

definitions.meaning: slight touches or tinges of something
medicines dissolved in spirit, such as iodine solution

explanation.surface: Small amounts of narcotics are found in a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means slight hints of something, and also medicinal extracts dissolved in spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both faint tinges and medicinal solutions made with spirit, two separate senses.

clue.text: Shade of colour found in shed

definitions.meaning: a tinge or tint, as in a greenish one
to throw off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.surface: A painter spots a faint tint inside a garden outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a hut where the colour was found, but it is a verb: to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a slight tinge of hue and to throw off or discard, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Crop of sentimental films from Bollywood?

definitions.text: Crop of sentimental films from Bollywood?

parts.words: Crop of sentimental films from Bollywood?
parts.note: the name of a cereal crop read as a description of mawkish, over-sentimental cinema from the Indian film industry

explanation.surface: A critic sneers at a harvest of soppy movies from the Mumbai studios.
explanation.walkthrough: Bollywood is the Hindi film industry based in Mumbai; 'sentimental' suggests 'corny', so its films would be corny Indian ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is known as this crop, and sentimental films from India would be corny Indian ones.

clue.text: General disapproval following introduction of party's platform

indicators.note: following places the synonym for disapproval after the first letter
the introduction of a word is its opening letter, here the start of party's

parts.note: odium is widespread hatred or disapproval

explanation.surface: A party's political programme is met with widespread contempt from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'platform' looks like a party manifesto, but it is the raised stand; 'following' puts ODIUM after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is a raised stand for a speaker or conductor, a small stage.

clue.text: The actor oddly cast as the Mikado, for instance

indicators.note: something oddly cast is set out in a strange arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A performer has been bizarrely chosen to play the Japanese emperor in an operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mikado is the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta's title emperor, and in Japan the emperor was held divine; 'oddly cast' rearranges THE ACTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler governing as a god or in the name of one, as the Japanese emperor was regarded, is an example.

clue.text: Hypocrite giving kisses to females in turn

parts.note: pecks are quick light kisses

indicators.note: turn means the letters for females and in are read backwards together

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, so FF stands for females
taken as written

explanation.surface: A two-faced man hands out kisses to one woman after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses FF and IN together to give NIFF. Pecksniff is the sanctimonious hypocrite in Dickens's novel Martin Chuzzlewit.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth Pecksniff in Dickens is a byword for unctuous sanctimony, so his name means a humbug.

clue.text: Mark of rank given to key NCO

parts.note: a pip is a star worn on the shoulder to show an officer's rank
E major is a musical key

explanation.surface: A soldier's insignia is awarded to an important non-commissioned officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like an adjective meaning important, but it is a musical key; a pipe major leads a military pipe band.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of a regimental pipe band holds a non-commissioned rank, typically a sergeant.

clue.text: Tom needs to soften up an agricultural worker

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the synonym for soften is written bottom to top

parts.note: to melt is to soften, as with butter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Tom must charm a farmhand into being friendlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name but it is a male cat; 'soften up' is the phrase for winning someone over, yet 'up' reverses MELT to TLEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who rears or tends livestock on a farm or ranch is a farm labourer of that kind.

clue.text: Bird appears to be doubly amorous

parts.note: to spoon is to kiss and cuddle
to bill, as in bill and coo, is to kiss and fondle

explanation.surface: A bird seems twice as affectionate as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' says two words for being amorous are joined: to spoon and to bill, as in 'bill and coo'.
explanation.definitionFit: This wading bird is named for its long flat bill with a broad rounded tip.

clue.text: Wandering in interior, aren't I going astray?

annotationWithheld.why: Wandering in interior, aren't I going astray? (9): the letters of IN and AREN'T I give only eight of the nine letters, lacking a T; no parse uses 'interior' for it and a search found no corrected text
annotationWithheld.clue: Wandering in interior, aren't I going astray?

clue.text: A state in the East with queen as ruler

parts.note: ME is the abbreviation for the US state of Maine
E is the abbreviation for east
R, for Regina, is the standard abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A monarch from the Orient travels to an American state with his consort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here, not a container sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An ameer, or emir, is a Muslim prince or governor, a title of sovereignty.

clue.text: Court woman love

annotationWithheld.why: Court woman love (5): PAT (woman) and O (love) give only four letters of PATIO; the I is missing, so a word such as 'I' seems lost from the clue as held

clue.text: 49/50 points featured in complaints

parts.note: IL is 49 and L is 50 in Roman numerals
N, E, S, S, E and S are compass points

explanation.surface: Almost all the issues raised appear among the grievances.
explanation.walkthrough: '49/50' looks like a near-perfect score but reads as two Roman numerals, IL and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints in the medical sense are ailments or disorders.

clue.text: Token number — a thousand — in Alabama

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
taken as written
AL is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Alabama

explanation.surface: A symbolic figure of one thousand is recorded in an American southern state.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominal or token payment is a small symbolic one, far below the real value.

clue.text: Just fire first trombone

indicators.note: first means the synonym for fire comes before the synonym for just

parts.note: to fire someone from a job is to sack them
just, as in merely or only, means but

explanation.surface: A bandleader dismisses the brass player before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just fire' reads as a blunt order to dismiss someone; 'first' tells you the word for fire goes ahead of the word for just.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is the early Renaissance form of the trombone.

clue.text: Every summer blowing up one place in eastern part of Mediterranean

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the place name is written bottom to top

parts.note: Sete is a port on France's Mediterranean coast
one is I, the Roman numeral
the eastern end of the written word, its last two letters

explanation.surface: Each summer a gale sweeps a town in the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing up' looks like one phrase, but 'up' reverses SETE to give ETES. The word describes the north winds that blow over the Aegean each summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Etesian means annual or periodic, used of the Mediterranean winds that recur each summer.

clue.text: To feign sickness is not entirely abnormal in geriatrics

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the phrase is used, so the letters sit inside these words

explanation.surface: Faking illness is not wholly out of the ordinary among elderly patients.
explanation.definitionFit: To shirk duty by pretending to be ill is exactly what the verb means.

clue.text: Mouse taken by pranksters

definitions.meaning: the cartoon mouse created by Walt Disney
to take the ... is to tease or make fun of someone

explanation.surface: A rodent is snatched by practical jokers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take the mickey' is British slang for mocking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's famous cartoon rodent bears this name, and jokers take it in the British idiom for teasing.

clue.text: Novel country pub

parts.note: Jamaica is a Caribbean island country
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A new tavern in a far-off land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it is the book: Daphne du Maurier's Cornish smuggling story.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne du Maurier's 1936 book is titled after a coaching tavern on Bodmin Moor.

clue.text: Nocturnal creature I caught — using this?

definitions.text: Nocturnal creature I caught — using this?

indicators.note: caught means the letter I is held inside the word for the creature

parts.note: a bat is a creature that flies at night

explanation.surface: An angler or trapper boasts of catching a night animal and wonders what lure did it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' puts I inside BAT, and the whole clue asks what was used to lure the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Food set out to lure an animal or fish into a trap or onto a hook is the lure meant.

clue.text: Locks of sterling construction

indicators.note: a construction is something put together, so the letters of sterling are built into a new order

explanation.surface: Doors with locks of real quality, solidly built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' looks like door fastenings and 'sterling' like praise for good work, but the locks are curls of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Curly tresses of hair are locks in the sense of hanks or curls.

clue.text: Landed after flight — with some prayers

parts.note: a bird that has landed after flying has alighted, or lit
some, as in any at all, means any

explanation.surface: A traveller lands safely and says a few prayers of thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a series of petitions recited in church, a form of prayer.
